goal.title: Everything falls out of the blueprint, for every building block in every output
goal.summary: Fifteen building blocks by nine outputs, 135 cards, each an eval with a stated green and stated evidence. Done is every card green or agreed not needed, then one story proves it whole: a fresh folder, the real ortho command, a new project, and the Plugged In app grown through its four stages.
writeUp: **What Orthograph promises.** You write a blueprint: the things your app keeps, the operations that change them, the steps each operation takes, the machine each thing moves through, the events a move emits, the errors a call can be refused with, the roles allowed to call, which fields are private or secret, the environments and stores it runs in, the plugins it mounts, where an operation runs, the clock and the moves made by time, and the journeys that prove it works. Everything else falls out of that one declaration for free: the model, the HTTP API, the server, the SDK, the CLI, the MCP tools, the docs, the portal and the telemetry. Nothing is configured twice, and nothing an output shows is written by hand.

**Why a grid measures it.** "Falls out for free" is a claim about every pair of building block and output. The coverage audit of 19 November (K12) drew that as a grid of 15 building blocks (13 at the audit, then invariants, G5, and time, K23) by 9 outputs, 135 cells, and found the claim fully true only for operations. A promise that holds for one row is not yet the promise. So the grid is the goal: each row is a lane, each cell in it is a card, and each card is an eval. A card says, in one or two sentences, what green means for that building block in that output, and names the evidence that proves it: an e2e check, a journey run through that output, or a view in the portal. A card is green only when its evidence runs in CI and passes. A card that exists in code but has no evidence is not green; it is "built, unproved", and the board shows it amber.

**What "done" looks like.** Every card is green, or Aaron has agreed it is not needed by design. A "not needed" card is not deleted: it stays on the board, greyed, with the one-line reason, so nobody reopens it by accident and anyone can see the grid is whole. Where an absence is itself a safety property (no secret field leaves through any output, no step leaks into a client's contract), the card stays live and its evidence proves the absence. When the last card turns green, the end-to-end story below runs from a fresh folder through all four stages of the Plugged In app, and the grid stays green after it.

**How it relates to the gates.** The grid does not replace the milestones; it is how we see them. Gate M1 (M1.15) is the first band: the basics of things, operations, steps, machines, events and errors in every output (K13's 5 by 5, M1.41 and M1.42), one visibility rule (M1.35), telemetry that carries the model (M1.36), and the portal as a viewer (M1.13). Gate M2, "workable" (M2.12, also the stage 1 gate), is the second: roles and principals (M2.01 to M2.07), secrets by declaration (M2.04), journeys run through the SDK, CLI and MCP (M2.08) so those three columns are proved by journeys rather than by hand-picked calls, `ortho new` (M2.09) so the story can start from nothing, and `ortho add` for the blocks that edit files in place (M2.14 to M2.16). The v1.0 stages fill the rest: stage 2 (ST2.06) the device lane and the adapter half of the mount lane, stage 3 (ST3.08) stores on a chain and workflows, stage 4 (ST4.08) the visibility lane at its hardest, a club whose members never show. The lanes this grid does not have yet (workflows, views, agents, chains as stores) join it as rows when their milestone's decision slice names their outputs; until then they are listed under "Rows still to come".

**How we use it.** The board shows one lane per row, its cards left to right in the column order below, each card green, amber (built, unproved), red (missing) or grey (not needed, agreed). Work is picked by lane, not by cell: a lane is climbed until it is fully green, so at each step we know exactly which building block is whole. The order is under "Hill-climb order".
goal.doneWhen: Every cell is green, or not-needed with Aaron's reason; then the story check runs from a fresh folder through all four stages of the Plugged In app and the grid stays green.

blocks.name: Operation & read
blocks.summary: An operation changes things; a read returns them. Each declares its payload, answer, who may call, idempotency and budget.

endState.title: The operation's page and the operations matrix
endState.description: Every operation and read is one endpoint, one SDK function, one CLI command, one MCP tool, one docs page and one portal page, with its description, who may call, its idempotency and its budget, and every call is counted and traced.

blocks.proof: The operation's page in the portal (the in-and-out band, the spine, the proof tab with its journeys' verdicts) and the operations matrix on home (calls, refused, defects, p95 against budget); journeys through each client (M2.08).
blocks.audiencesBecause: The caller's whole contract, the builder's handler, the operator's calls and budget.

blocks.name: Error & refusal code
blocks.summary: A refusal a call can end in: a declared error, the wrong-state refusal, NotAllowed, each with a code and an exit.

endState.title: Refusals on the arrows, in the band, counted by code
endState.description: Every refusal a caller can get, declared or the runtime's own, has a name, a code and an exit, and the same three reach the SDK as a typed class, the CLI as `[code] Name` and its exit, MCP as an error with its code, the docs' refusals table, the portal's arrows and counts, and the span.

blocks.proof: Refusals on the arrow they guard and in the in-and-out band, counted by code (portal.md); M1.41's refused claim prints `HN-001`; `refusal.code` on the span (M1.36).
blocks.audiencesBecause: Refusals are the caller's contract: name, code and exit.

blocks.name: Thing & fields
blocks.summary: A thing the app keeps, with its fields: their types, references, optionality, visibility and description.

endState.title: Home's thing cards and each thing's page
endState.description: Every thing the blueprint declares, with every field's type, reference, optionality, visibility and description, is the same in every output: typed in the SDK, a typed and described flag in the CLI, an input and output schema in MCP, a reference page in the docs, and a card and page in the portal.

blocks.proof: The portal's home (one card per thing, grouped by `from`) and each thing's page, with the in-and-out band showing every field and its visibility; M1.41 reads every output for each thing's type and fields; the stage 1 journeys run through the SDK, CLI and MCP (M2.08).
blocks.audiencesBecause: A thing's fields are every payload and answer: callers type against them, builders declare them, operators see them on spans.

blocks.name: Step
blocks.summary: A step an operation takes in order: database, wait or call, with the stores it writes and whether it is optional.

endState.title: The operation's spine
endState.description: Every declared step (its kind, the stores it writes, whether it is optional, and the adapter it calls) is in the model, run in order by the server, documented, drawn on the operation's spine and traced as its own span, and never part of a client's contract.

blocks.proof: The operation's spine in the portal: each declared step in its place, a finished call's spans down it, a running call's step signals as they arrive (M1.21); `ortho prove --empty` shows one red step per blank.
blocks.audiencesBecause: How the handler works, not what the caller asked for: a step renamed or split must never change a caller's contract. Leaving its audience is a leak, so its caller cards are absence checks.

blocks.name: Machine, states, move
blocks.summary: A thing's lifecycle: its states, the moves between them, what each move emits.

endState.title: The lifecycle strip on a thing's card and page
endState.description: A thing's lifecycle (its states, its moves, what each move emits and the refusal for a wrong state) is typed in every client, documented, drawn as the lifecycle strip in the portal, and every move is traced from and to.

blocks.proof: The lifecycle strip on a thing's card and page, with move counts on each arrow and refusals on the arrow they guard (portal.md, "A thing's page"), lit by `move.name`, `move.from` and `move.to`.
blocks.audiencesBecause: A thing's state is in its answers, and the wrong-state refusal is the first thing a caller meets; the moves are the builder's, the transitions on spans the operator's.

blocks.name: Event
blocks.summary: A fact a move emits, with its fields, committed to the journal with the move.

endState.title: Events on a thing's page and on the spine's commit
endState.description: Every event a move emits is typed in the SDK, documented with its fields, shown on the thing's page with its fields, named on the commit span, and its committed occurrences show in the portal with the commit that wrote them.

blocks.proof: The thing's page lists its events with their fields; an operation's spine shows the event its commit emitted and the `on:` handlers it set off (M1.21's committed events from the journal).
blocks.audiencesBecause: The runtime's record of a move, read by the builder and the operator. A caller reads state, not the journal, until views make events followable (M5.05, Q3).

blocks.name: Field visibility (secret, private)
blocks.summary: Who may see a field: public by default, private to roles, or secret.

endState.title: The band's secret and private marks, and the no-leak check
endState.description: One rule decides, per audience, what each field shows: a secret leaves only in the answer of the call that issued it, a private field only to the roles it names, and every output (HTTP answers and refusals, SDK, CLI, MCP, docs, portal, spans, journal, logs) calls the same rule and fails closed.

blocks.proof: Check 16 renders every output for every audience over a fixture with a public, a private and a secret field (M1.35); the portal's "no leak" check (M1.13); stage 4's club, whose portal shows nothing that names a member (ST4.07).
blocks.audiencesBecause: The rule over what each audience sees: its caller cards are where a secret must not leave.

blocks.name: Journey & starting world
blocks.summary: A scripted story with a cast, run against a starting world, that proves the operations work.

endState.title: The proof tab on each operation
endState.description: Every journey and starting world is in the model, runs through each client (SDK, CLI, MCP), is listed in the docs as the worked example of the operations it covers, and shows in the portal as the proof on each operation, its runs lighting up what it touched.

blocks.proof: The proof tab on each operation (the journeys that cover it and their verdicts, M1.04) and the proof matrix per environment (portal.md); `ortho prove` passing `--through sdk|cli|mcp` (M2.08).
blocks.audiencesBecause: Journeys prove the app: they run through the clients (M2.08), never in them. The server's part is the starting world, gated to environments with a lifetime.

blocks.name: Roles
blocks.summary: Who may call an operation: anyone, signed in, or a role of the thing, with its rule.

endState.title: Roles on a thing's page and `allowed` in each band
endState.description: Who may call each operation is declared once and is true everywhere: enforced by the server, said in the SDK's doc comment, the CLI's help and the MCP tool's description, MCP lists only the tools the caller's roles allow, the docs and portal show each role rule, and each span says which role let the call through.

blocks.proof: Roles on a thing's page and `allowed` in each operation's band (portal.md); the stage 1 journeys "a stranger can't edit" run through every client (ST1.02 with M2.08); M2.02's principal journeys.
blocks.audiencesBecause: A caller needs to know who may call before calling (M2.03); a refusal says NotAllowed.

blocks.name: Environment
blocks.summary: Where the app runs: local, test, staging, production, each with its identity, stores, secrets, sink and domains.

endState.title: The environment switcher and the proof matrix
endState.description: Each declared environment (where it runs, its identity, its stores' bindings, its secrets by name, its telemetry sink, its domains) is served as declared, named on every call's span, documented, and is the portal's switcher; whether the clients know environments by name is Q4.

blocks.proof: The portal's environment switcher in the top bar and the proof matrix (every operation against every environment, portal.md "Environments"); `environment` on every span (M1.36).
blocks.audiencesBecause: Where the app runs and what it binds is the builder's and the operator's; a caller is handed a URL. Q4 decides whether the caller gets the environments' names and public domains.

blocks.name: Store
blocks.summary: Where things live: a database or actor store, bound per environment, one per commit.

endState.title: The data page and a thing's store in its header
endState.description: Each store the blueprint declares (or a mounted plugin brings) has its own binding and migrations, says what lives in it in the docs and the portal's data page, and is named on every call's span; callers never see where a thing lives.

blocks.proof: The portal's data page (every store, its kind, binding and migrations, M5.06) and a thing's header naming its store; `store` on every span (M1.36); K3's check that a call writing two stores is refused (Gate M1 item 5).
blocks.audiencesBecause: Where things live: a store renamed or rebound must never change a caller's contract.

blocks.name: Mount, adapter, plugin origin
blocks.summary: A plugin mounted with one file: a feature, adapter or projection, with its package and version.

endState.title: The tree grouped by plugin, and call steps naming their adapter
endState.description: A plugin mounted with one file brings its things, operations, stores and adapters into every output as if they were the app's own, honouring the mount's narrowing, while the docs, the portal and the spans say where each came from (plugin, package, version) and which adapter a call step called.

blocks.proof: The portal's tree, one folded group per mounted plugin with its version in the page header (portal.md, "The frame"); a call step on the spine naming its adapter; check 01 mounts a plugin with one command (Gate M1 item 1).
blocks.audiencesBecause: A mounted plugin's operations reach callers through the operation lane, as the app's own; which plugin they came from is the builder's and the operator's.

blocks.name: Runs on the device (runs: "client")
blocks.summary: An operation declared `runs: "client"`: it runs in the caller's process, never on the server.

endState.title: The operation's page marked on your device
endState.description: An operation declared `runs: "client"` runs in the caller's process from the SDK and the CLI with no server request, never on the server, is documented as running on the device, marked in the portal, and its spans reach the environment's sink like any call.

blocks.proof: Check 11 (a client operation through the SDK and CLI with no server call); stage 2's wallet created on the device (ST2.06); the operation's page in the portal marked "on your device", lit by its spans (portal.md gap 4).
blocks.audiencesBecause: The caller runs a device operation in its own process; the builder declares it, the operator sees its spans (ST2.07).

blocks.name: Invariants (unique rules, G5)
blocks.summary: A thing's rule that stays true among many records of it: `Blueprint.invariant.unique(field or tuple, { while, refuse, description })` in `things/<thing>/invariants.ts`; the runtime refuses for the handler.

endState.title: The thing's page and the operation's page show the rules
endState.description: A rule is declared once in `invariants.ts`, and every output says it: each operation that can break it lists the rule's refusal, the runtime refuses and the span names the rule, the docs and the MCP tool say why in one sentence, and the portal's page for the thing shows a Rules section that each refusal links back to.

blocks.proof: Check 25 (the model, the compiler's refusals, a real world, the outputs) and its package halves; check 31 (S-19, a value moving between holders); `ortho prove` on Plugged In's claim journey, which refuses both rules; ST1.22's Chromium check on the portal's Rules section.
blocks.audiencesBecause: The caller meets the rule's refusal in every client; the builder declares it and reads its sentence in the docs; the operator sees which rule refused in the spans and the portal.

blocks.name: Time (the world's clock, moves made by time)
blocks.summary: One clock per world drives everything in it; a move can be made by time (`every`, `after`) and a journey can step the clock.

endState.title: The world's time beside the real one, and each timed move's lateness
endState.description: A world has one clock that the server, the database, every Timers wait, the chain and the adapters share. A journey steps it with `s.clock`, `ortho clock` moves it by hand in a dev world, a move declared `by: every` or `after` happens exactly once at its due instant within `late`, and the docs, the MCP tools, the portal and the spans say when.

blocks.proof: Gate M8 (`nx run e2e:m8`): a month renews once (M8.02), the world's clock reads the same everywhere (M8.03), moves made by time and the on-time eval (M8.04, M8.12); the portal's world bar shows the world's time and each move's lateness (M8.13).
blocks.audiencesBecause: The builder declares the clock and the timed moves and steps it in journeys; the operator runs and watches it; a caller meets it in `ortho clock`, in the tool descriptions that say when a move happens, and in the SDK a journey drives.

story.summary: One run in a fresh folder: npm create orthograph plugged-in, ortho generate and prove, every operation through the SDK, CLI and MCP, the portal lit by a claim, then handles and auth mounted, then stages 2 to 4.

steps.step: `npm create orthograph plugged-in` in an empty folder
steps.proves: the front door works with no checkout of this repository
steps.describedBy: M2.09 (`ortho new` scaffolds Plugged In at stage 1, identical to `examples/plugged-in`)

steps.proves: every output is written and every journey passes on workerd
steps.lanes: thing, operation, step, machine, event, error, roles, journey
steps.describedBy: M1.41 (the loop through the real `ortho` binary), M2.12
steps.gap: M1.41 copies `examples/plugged-in` into the folder; the story starts from `ortho new` instead, so the two meet only at M2.09

steps.step: the server runs; every operation is called once through the SDK, the CLI and MCP; a refused claim prints `HN-001` and exits 3
steps.proves: the surfaces tier, for every lane in stage 1
steps.lanes: the surfaces columns of every stage 1 lane
steps.gap: M1.41 calls no MCP tool; M2.08 brings it

steps.step: the portal opens on Plugged In's things; a claim lights `handle.claim` and its move, its event, its commit; the proof tab shows the journeys' verdicts
steps.lanes: docs, portal, telemetry of every stage 1 lane
steps.describedBy: M1.13 (the portal opens on Plugged In's things, a journey's run lights its operation and move)
steps.gap: the portal wire still says traces and journeys are "unavailable" (`packages/portal/src/modules/wire/service.ts:6-9`)

steps.step: `ortho add feature @orthograph/handles`, then auth (ST1.03, ST1.07); the grid stays green
steps.proves: mounting keeps the promise: a mounted plugin's blocks reach every output with their `from`
steps.gap: no check reads every output for a mounted block's `from`

steps.step: stage 2: `ortho add feature @orthograph/wallets`; create a wallet on the device; be paid by handle on Anvil; a reorg corrects it
steps.proves: device operations, adapters, chain events, environments with a chain
steps.lanes: device, mount (adapters), event (from the follower), environment
steps.gap: the device lane's CLI, MCP and portal cards have no slice (see that lane)

steps.step: stage 3: a Safe with the budgets plugin, hats, owners sign above a budget
steps.proves: stores on a chain, workflows, agents under their own hat
steps.lanes: store, roles (hats), and the rows still to come
steps.gap: workflows and agents are not rows yet

steps.step: stage 4: the same on Aztec; the portal shows the footprint and never a member
steps.describedBy: ST4.08 (`the portal shows nothing that names a member`, ST4.07)
steps.gap: none beyond the stage's own slices

story.missing: Nothing yet runs the stages in one folder from nothing, and nothing reads the grid at each step.
story.proposedSlice: The story check (e2e/story), after Gate M2, written by an author who is not the builder: steps 1 to 5 through the real ortho binary, writing one verdict per card to the logbook (kind grid, keyed by card id and revision); steps 6 to 8 appended as each stage gate lands.

questions.recommendation: A: yes, with the table as written

questions.recommendation: A: not until views (M5.05); M1.42's SDK event types move there
